data.theorem_title: Log–log plot of the Zipf distribution is affine with slope $-s$
data.formal_statement:
namespace ZipfLaw

theorem log_zipfPMF_affine (N : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk1 : 1 ≤ k) (hkN : k ≤ N) :
    Real.log (zipfPMF N s k) = -s * Real.log k - Real.log (genHarmonic N s) := by sorry

end ZipfLaw
data.natural_language_statement:
For $1\le k\le N$ and real $s$,
$$\ln f(k;N,s)=-s\ln k-\ln H_{N,s},$$
so on a log–log plot (log rank against log frequency) the Zipf distribution lies on a straight line of slope $-s$.
data.source: Wikipedia, "Zipf's law" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipf%27s_law), snapshot uploaded by the proposer, section "Empirical testing" ("The data conform to Zipf's law with exponent s to the extent that the plot approximates a linear (more precisely, affine) function with slope −s").
